newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Penis-shrinker scare hits Ivory Coast, two killed.
newsitem.headline: Penis-shrinker scare hits Ivory Coast, two killed.

text.p: Angry mobs burned or beat to death at least two alleged sorcerers in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan after a shrinking or disappearing penis scare spread from neighbouring Ghana.
Police or witnesses confirmed details of Thursday's killings and related incidents on Friday, when crowds gathered in many parts of the city to flush out and chase suspects.
Police commanders ordered that all impromptu gatherings be dispersed in an effort to prevent the attacks spreading.

Round the corner from the U.S. embassy in the city centre, witnesses saw one alleged sorcerer flee into a nearby police station for protection as youths hurled stones. Amused bystanders looked on, young men covering their genitals with their hands.

Such reports are not uncommon in West or Central Africa. Purported victims often blame handshakes with sorcerers. At least 12 men were killed in Ghana in January by mobs accusing them of making penises shrink or vanish.
Police in Ghana and Ivory Coast dismiss the phenomenon as a ploy by thieves to cause a crowd to form and then rob people.

The dead in Abidjan appeared to be Hausa, a major tribe in northern Nigeria with representatives in many West Africa countries. One police source said there had been clashes between Hausa and Ivorians in the teeming Yopougon suburb on Friday.

Ivorian police said one alleged sorcerer was covered in petrol and set alight in Abidjan's populous Koumassi suburb and a second beaten to death in Port Bouet on the outskirts of the city. A mob seriously hurt a third man in Marcory suburb.
Witnesses reported a second man burnt to death in Koumassi but there was no official confirmation.

In a fourth incident, secondary school students demonstrated outside a local police station in Yopougon on Thursday, demanding action against a stranger they accused of making a fellow student's penis disappear.
The students had chased the man to the police station, where he took refuge, police said.
Victims say sorcerers simply touch them and make their penises to shrink or vanish by witchcraft to extort cash in return for a cure.

Similar cases have been reported in Ivory Coast in recent weeks but until Thursday no deaths. State television carried details of one case on its main evening news on Wednesday, quoting a victim in a light-hearted report.
The independent newspaper Le Jour carried a front-page photograph of the charred Koumassi body and quoted witnesses as saying that the man had been burned as a sorcerer.
Residents in Accra recall a similar scare in the early 1980s. They attributed the scale of the crisis there to the fact that genitals are used in certain voodoo rituals.
Ghana state television interviewed experts on the subject who explained in minute medical detail how and why penises shrink or expand.
